methodology.Fees: The tax ArgusPad's per-launch hook charges on every buy and sell, the trading fee each launch's pool charges (on Portals 3-7 the 1% pool fee earned by the permanently locked launch position; on Portal 8 a 1% base fee the hook charges in the quote asset in its place), and the extra tax charged on buys in a launch's first seconds. Counted in the asset the fee is charged in, at the moment it is charged, so the protocol's later sale of the launched tokens it was paid is not counted a second time. Fees charged in the launched token itself (Portals 3-7 only; Portal 8 takes every fee in the quote asset) are reported in that token's own units and are priced only if DefiLlama has a price for it; it has none for these tokens today, because a launched token's only market is the pool ArgusPad seeded, and pricing it there overstates by about 40% against what ArgusPad's own sales of them actually realise.
methodology.Revenue: The share of fees reaching the ArgusPad treasury at the rate each launch fixes at creation - 10% of every fee on Portals 3-7 and 30% on Portal 8 - plus the whole of the early-buy snipe tax, which is paid straight to the treasury.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The share of fees reaching the ArgusPad treasury at the rate each launch fixes at creation - 10% of every fee on Portals 3-7 and 30% on Portal 8 - plus the whole of the early-buy snipe tax, which is paid straight to the treasury.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The rest of the fees, which leave the protocol divided at the weights each launch fixed at creation: the token creator's share, the dividends paid to holders of that launched token, the share added back into the launch's permanently locked liquidity, the share used to buy and burn the launched token, and on Portal 8 the share used to buy the launched token and lock it permanently.

methodology.Fees: The tax BaseStonk's Uniswap v4 hook takes on every swap in a launched token's pool, from the hook's FeeTaken event. Each launch sets its own buy and sell rate. A buy pays the tax in the launch token and a sell in the pair; token-denominated amounts are converted into the pair at the pool price the same transaction's Swap reports.
methodology.Revenue: The platform's cut of the tax plus what reaches BSTONK holders: half the tax capped at 1% of the trade to the treasury, any part of the creator's cut the payee list left unplaced and the hook swept to the treasury, and the share of the creator's cut paid to BSTONK's dividend distributor, to the BSTONK basket vault, or burnt as BSTONK.
methodology.ProtocolRevenue: The treasury's take: half the tax capped at 1% of the trade, plus unplaced creator fees swept to it.
methodology.HoldersRevenue: Value to BSTONK holders, paid by the hook in the transaction the fee was taken: BSTONK's own pool pays its creator cut to BSTONK's dividend distributor and burns half of it, and launches carry the BSTONK basket vault as a payee; the vault pays BSTONK holders in rounds. Base only - BSTONK lives on Base.
methodology.SupplySideRevenue: The creator's cut of the tax less what the treasury swept and what reached BSTONK holders: the creator's wallets, the launch token's own holders through its dividend distributor, the burn of the launch token and the hook-owned liquidity wedge, as each launch configured them.
methodology.Volume: The pair side of every swap in a taxed pool, including the creator's dev buy at launch and excluding the hook's own buyback and liquidity swaps. Counted under Uniswap v4 as well.

discovery.note: Codex launchpad names validated 2026-09-28 against its error message listing valid names. foci, Graphite, Binance Alpha, StonkBrokers, RapidLaunch and BaseStonk have no Codex launchpad name and are not swept. Sweeps run per chain group so busy Solana tokens do not crowd out EVM launchpads (validated 2026-10-02: EVM rows 33 -> 140). trendingScore24 ranking validated 2026-10-02. trendQueries are broad X searches run daily in e1 (2026-10-02: "memecoin meta" and "four.meme meta" surfaced the Super Intelligence wave; "new meta pump.fun" and "narrative memecoins" returned mostly call-group spam and were dropped) to surface stories the token sweep has not clustered yet; maxClusters bounds discover.py theme clusters. maxClusterWordShare drops theme words shared by more candidates than this (generic words such as fees or earn); shared tickers are never capped.

scout.note: Hourly scout (docs/prompts/scout.md, scripts/frames-refresh/scout.py). plan.py scout writes the d1 sweep above plus a <group>_fresh alias per chain group: tokens created within freshWindowHours with 24h volume above narrativeRules.addMember.minVolume24Usd, so new coins surface hours old instead of waiting for recentMinVolumeUsd. A new coin is listed while its first pool is at most newCoinHours old and it meets the addMember bar without a quarantine flag. A theme cluster is shown only after an X search in the same scout run finds a public source for its story (status confirmed), or once the daily run tracks it (tracked). Confirmed leads stay listed keepConfirmedHours after they were last seen, tracked ones keepTrackedHours; rejected and deferred decisions are remembered rememberDecisionsHours so the same theme is not paid for again, and are re-checked only after recheckAfterHours (rejected ones also need recheckVolumeMultiple times the volume they were rejected at).

newNarrative.evidence: Each constituent: exact chain + address, covered launchpad, and either its own token metadata (name, symbol or description) naming the story or mechanism itself, or an official source naming the coin in connection with the story. A word the coin merely shares with the story's theme does not count (for example 'Pokémon' or 'collector' for Pump.fun's card-gacha integration). Quote the metadata or cite the source for each constituent in curation.newMembers; minConstituents counts only coins that meet this. The story: at least one independent public source (official page or X post) beyond token metadata.
newNarrative.correction: A narrative created without meeting this bar is corrected on the next run. Record it in curation.retiredNarratives with the reason 'created without meeting the newNarrative bar: <what was missing>'; this closes its memberships, and its pages stay reachable with the reason. Remove its pools from poolUniverse, and resume any narrative paused only to make room for it.
newNarrative.daily: Every run evaluates every theme cluster discover.py reports and records a decision in curation.clusterDecisions (created, assigned, rejected or deferred, with a reason). Create a narrative whenever a cluster or a story meets this bar. maxActive caps how many narratives are collected and featured, not how many exist: at the cap, pause the weakest (curation.pausedNarratives) only when the new one has more 24h volume and its story is current. A paused narrative keeps its memberships and pages; it is not retired.

addMember.evidence: Same evidence bar as a new narrative constituent.

removeMember.evidence: Below the threshold on two consecutive observations: archive the coin (curation.archivedMembers) — collection stops, the membership interval stays open and the coin's pages stay reachable. Evidence that contradicts membership (for example removal from an official registry): curation.removedMembers closes the interval. Never delete the record.

retireNarrative.evidence: Below the threshold on two consecutive observations: pause collection (curation.pausedNarratives); memberships stay open. Retire (curation.retiredNarratives, closes memberships) only when the defining source is gone or contradicted. Record the reason either way.

quarantine.evidence: Flagged tokens are never constituents; record them as quarantined candidates.

storyChecks.note: Every X search in the run counts: e1's dailyEvidence and trendQueries searches (up to 10 with its pages), discover.py stories' cluster theme searches (up to 10), and targeted follow-ups, which get at least 4. Each X search is about 7 credits; each page scrape about 5.
